subject: Benchmark readout & latency results — multi-team scheduling
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex@redwood.ai>

Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Date: Sun, 10 May 2026 14:02:00 -0700
Subject: Benchmark readout & latency results — multi-team scheduling

Hi Carlos,

Thanks again for running the test workloads last week — the preliminary token-level breakdown looks promising. We'd like to do a 45-60 minute readout to walk through:

- Key latency percentiles (p50/p95/p99) across the three model variants
- End-to-end throughput with your batch pattern and concurrency
- Recommendations (batching, KV-cache, quant) and expected cost delta
- Open issues / follow-ups for your security and procurement teams

Can we get the right set of folks together for a single readout? Proposed attendees from our side: myself (AE), Marissa (CS), and Karthik (SE). Please include whoever from engineering, procurement, and security on your side.

I attached the rough benchmark spreadsheet and the config snapshot we used for the run. Suggested slots (PDT):
- Tue May 12, 10:00–11:00
- Wed May 13, 14:00–15:00
- Thu May 14, 09:00–10:00

If those don't work, let me know a couple windows and we'll accommodate.

Attachments: [Attachment: benchmark_results_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 1.2MB)], [Attachment: redwood_latency_config.json (text, 12KB)]

Thanks,
Alex Martinez
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
alex@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192

Alex — thanks, this looks useful.

I can be available: Tue May 12 at 10:00 PDT works for our backend lead (we'll convert timezones). Priya (procurement) and Maya (security) are cc'd — can they confirm? A couple quick asks from our side so the readout is productive:

- We'll need a clear slide/section that lists what metric definitions you used (how p95/p99 were computed)
- Any shared test artifacts (scripts or synthetic load generator) should be linked so our infra team can reproduce locally
- For procurement: an outline of the data flows and whether any customer payloads were persisted/escaped to Redwood logs.

If procurement wants to push PO/contract questions before the readout, we can do that in parallel but prefer the technical readout first.

—Carlos

Alex — procurement here. We can do Thu May 21 11:00–12:00 PDT. A couple procurement/security items before the readout:

- Can you confirm whether any production customer data was used in the benchmark? If so, we need a short data handling summary and retention guarantees.
- We will need the onboarding checklist / SOC-2 basics sent to procurement before we sign any mutual action plan.
- Please send an invoice template / indicative pricing for the dedicated capacity scenario you mentioned in the call (monthly commit + burst).

If you can share the one-page pre-read and the SOC-2 checklist by EOD Tuesday PDT, we can review ahead of the readout.

Great — Thu May 21, 11:00 PDT is confirmed from our side. I'll lead the technical readout and cover:

- How we compute percentiles (sliding-window, warmup removal), and the exact sample counts per run
- Repro steps and a minimal load script (I'll put a README + script in Drive)
- Data handling: no customer payload was persisted to third-party storage during the benchmark; logs were operational and contain only request-level metadata. I'll attach a short SOC-2 checklist and the config snapshot referenced earlier.

Action items before Wed EOD (PDT):
- Alex: please upload the 1-page pre-read to Drive and drop an invite (calendar .ics)
- Marissa: I'll need the canary prompt set and the diff of model variants for the readout slides
- Priya: if procurement can share any standard NDAs/PO terms you prefer, I'll make sure the readout clarifies the commercial options.

Attachments referenced: [Attachment: redwood_latency_config.json], [Attachment: benchmark_results_v1.xlsx], [Attachment: SOC2_checklist_short.pdf (pdf, 120KB)]

See you Thursday — I'll post the final calendar invite and add dial-in + timezone conversions.
